reviews.title: Not worth subscription
reviews.text: Premium subscription is extremely difficult to cancel - you must jump through hoops on the website rather than through the app or Apple. Customer service is unhelpful, and you continue to get ads while being subscribed to premium. You cannot cancel through apple or you will continue to be charged, and even if you click through the app and manage to find your transaction history, it will not include dates, which is very frustrating. You can’t even cancel within the app, only on the external developer’s website. Premium features are fine if you can get discount, but certainly not worth the money or headache especially considering annual billing means they will likely get an extra year’s payment out of you. So many features have also gotten so much worse in the last year. After some research, it looks like this subscription model may be against Apple’s policies, so other users leaving negative reviews about similar experiences should make a report to Apple as well.

If they replaced “stress” with “physiological activation” or “autonomic load,” the exact same data would feel completely different—and would be harder to misinterpret.

Likewise, instead of:

* Stress → physiological activation/load
* Fight-or-flight → sympathetic activity
* Rest-and-digest → parasympathetic activity
* Stress building up → activation accumulating
* Stress relieved → activation decreasing/recovery

That would make much more sense for you. You’ve spent almost two years seeing red screens essentially saying STRESS!, even when you didn’t feel stressed. So far, I’m impressed. One thing I really liked was the AI-guided setup. Instead of just throwing a wall of settings at you, it walks you through the process. For anyone who’s less tech-savvy (impatient with settings menus), that’s a nice touch.

The free version lets you see some meaningful information instead of immediately smacking you with a giant paywall every time you tap something. There’s more data locked behind Premium—standard for apps—but there’s enough available to let you decide whether it’s worth subscribing. 

Speaking of which… I’m leaning toward subscribing because I’m curious to see what the deeper insights are. That’s probably the biggest compliment I can give after only one day of use.

To make matters worse, I can’t even cancel the subscription. The app tells me to check my Apple subscriptions, but it isn’t listed there. The FAQ links to the website to manage billing, but when I log in it only shows a $0.00 one-time charge and no active subscription, even though I’ve been charged nearly $110. There is no clear way to stop the charges or contact someone who can actually resolve the issue.

My job is extremely physically demanding, but that doesn’t mean I’m not highly stressed. The app seems to mistake physical activity for low stress, making the data unreliable and not reflective of my actual health.

The misleading trial offer, unexpected charges, impossible cancellation process, lack of billing transparency, and inaccurate health data make this app impossible for me to recommend.

I’ve been using Welltory since around 2019. I have pulmonary hypertension, and I’m also a physician, so I appreciate both the clinical and technical aspects of health tracking. When it works, I genuinely believe Welltory is the best health analytics app available. I’ve recommended it to friends, family, colleagues, and even patients because I truly believe in the product.

The Apple Watch integration, Apple Health connectivity, HRV analysis, charts, insights, and educational content are outstanding. I’d still love to see additional integrations with smart scales and pulse oximeters, but overall the app is incredibly well designed.

The reason I’m giving 2 instead of 5 stars is because the subscription and customer support experience has become a mess.

I am.. or was a Premium subscriber for years, but for a very long time now my account has shown “Free” even though my purchase history shows previous annual subscriptions. Restore Purchases doesn’t work. It tells me I already have an account, yet I can’t access Premium.

To make matters even more confusing, I still have the Apple Watch app installed with all permissions enabled, but the iPhone app says my watch isn’t connected and then prompts me to buy Premium again.  Get my data is being loaded and I am accessing the app actively through my watch.

Getting help has been nearly impossible. The website provides very little information about my subscription history, and I couldn’t find a way to contact support for well over a year. I finally discovered the “Report a Problem” option after someone on an external discussion forum pointed it out. It’s extremely difficult to notice because it’s displayed in very dark gray text at the bottom of the menu.

The purchasing experience is also confusing and inconsistent. The app advertises discounted annual subscriptions, but when I tap the offer it redirects me to Welltory’s website. There, I can’t pay using my Apple ID/App Store balance. If I instead subscribe through the App Store so I can use my Apple account, the discounted pricing disappears and I’m only offered the full-price annual subscription. There’s also no monthly App Store subscription available. As a result, I have to choose between getting the advertised discount or paying through my Apple account—I can’t do both.

I genuinely believe Welltory is the best health analytics app available and still recommend to countless friends, family, and clients for this day. This review isn’t about the quality of the product—it’s about the subscription system, account recovery, and lack of accessible customer support. If those issues are resolved, I’ll gladly update this review back to 5 stars.
